chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ayyub ibn Nooh, who said, 'I heard Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon him) say:'

Whoever visits the shrine of his father (Imam al-Rida) in Toos, God will forgive him for what has preceded of his sins and what has followed. And on the Day of Resurrection, a pulpit will be set up for him in front of the pulpit of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), until God the Exalted finishes the reckoning of the servants.

key_terms.طُوسٍ: Toos, a city in Iran known for the shrine of Imam al-Rida
key_terms.قَبْرَ أَبِيهِ: The shrine of his father (referring to Imam al-Rida)
key_terms.مَنْبَرٌ: A pulpit or raised platform, symbolizing honor and status

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the shrine of Imam al-Rida in Toos according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this hadith underscores the unique spiritual status of Imam al-Rida (a.s.) within the Ahl al-Bayt, linking the act of Ziyarah to comprehensive forgiveness (from minor to major sins). The eschatological imagery of a pulpit (minbar) placed opposite the Prophet’s pulpit signifies a high rank of intercession and proximity to divine mercy, emphasizing that this honor persists until the final accounting of all creation is concluded.
